text.p: *** BIRTHDAYS ***
Physician EDWARD DAVY, who became a pioneer in Victoria and South Australia and invented an electric relay and a copper smelter, was born in 1806.
Australian politician JOHN MCELHONE, who promoted the need to increase Australia's population, was born in 1833.
Australian engineer WILLIAM KERNOTT, who was a professor at Melbourne University, was born in 1845.
English-born comedian STAN LAUREL (JEFFERSON), who built a successful film career in the United States with OLIVER HARDY, was born in 1890.
Australian aviator HENRY 'GOYER' HENRY, who became involved in New Guinea coastal shipping and lost a leg in an air crash, was born in 1901.
Leading English cricketer TOM GRAVENEY, considered one of the all time greatest British sportsmen, was born in 1927.
Aboriginal politician CHARLES NELSON PERKINS was born in 1936.
US country singer BILLY "CRASH" CRADDOCK was born in 1939. His most well-known hit was "Rub It In" (1974). He appeared in the country charts until 1983.
*** EVENTS ***

1487 : The last great battle was fought on English soil, signifying the end of the 'War of the Roses' between the houses of York and Lancaster. Six thousand soldiers died in the Battle of Stoke, which secured the English throne for the Tudor monarchs.
1819 : More than two thousand people were killed during a huge earthquake near Ponnah, in the East Indies.
1869 : English explorer CHARLER STURT, who uncovered much of Australia, died at the age of 74.
1880 : Salvation Army ladies wore their distinctive bonnets for the first time during a march in London.
1903 : The year old Pepsi Cola company registered its trade name as "Pepsi-Cola".
1929 : The first four places in the 24-hour Le Mans endurance race were won by 'Bentleys'.

1935 : American President FRANKLIN D. (DELANO) ROOSEVELT presented his 'new deal' legislative package, aimed at tackling the economic problems of the nation's depression. The package embodied old-age pensions, unemployment insurance and public health aid.

1948 : The first air hijacking was recorded, when Chinese bandits attempted to take-over control of a Cathay Airways (Catalina) flying boat. The aircraft crew fought back, resulting in the plane crashing. All on board, apart from the hijack leader, died.
1958 : The British introduced a system of marking yellow-lines on roadways, to indicate no-parking zones.

1961 : Star dancer with the Leningrad Ballet, RUDOLF NUREYEV, sought political asylum in France, after being forbidden at the last minute to fly with the rest of his troupe to London. The 23 year old was about to board the flight at Le Bourget Airport when officials from the Russian Embassy told him to return to Moscow. He ran to the nearest police officer and shouted "protect me".
1963 : VALENTINA TERESHKOVA blasted-off from the Soviet Union in a 'Vostok 6' rocket, to become the first woman in space.
1977 : German rocket pioneer WERNER VON BRAUN, who pursued his career under the Nazis and continued his work in the United States following World War Two, died.

1983 : Europe re-entered the space race, with the launch of a French 'Ariane One' rocket. The future of the space program had been put in doubt following crashes on the second and fifth Ariane missions.
1990 : Belgian Police arrested three I.R.A members, suspected of killing two Australians during an attack in Holland.
